Karl von Frisch and the bee language

The Austrian ethologist Karl von Frisch spent decades studying honeybees. In the 1940s he showed that the waggle dance tells other bees both the direction and the distance of food. His experiments moved feeding stations step by step and watched how the dances changed.

Von Frisch shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1973 with Konrad Lorenz and Nikolaas Tinbergen for discoveries about animal behaviour. His decoding of the dance is one of the best known results in the study of animal communication.

Some researchers later doubted that bees really used the information, but radar tracking experiments in the 2000s confirmed that recruits fly where the dance points.
